newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan Q&A -- Inflation, interest rates Part I.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan Q&A -- Inflation, interest rates Part I.

text.p: Following are excerpts from the question-and-answer session with Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan before the Senate Banking Committee, after the second day of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Sen. Sarbanes, (D-Md): "We've had six consecutive months of decline in the producer price index -- something that has not been seen since 1949. Isn't it reasonable to assume that these declines in producer prices will feed into slower inflation?"

Greenspan: "Remember, those are finished goods and they comprise both consumer goods and capital goods amongst a number of miscellaneous things. It's only the consumer goods part that tends to reflect itself in the goods part of the consumer price index.

But as you know, there is rather a significant services element within the consumer price index and indeed, services have been rising in somewhat of a faster pace, albeit a slowing pace, than goods price inflation. A goodly part of that decline, I might add, is the declining prices in capital goods, which become increasingly more computer-related, and, as a consequence, subject to increasing types of price declines which are so characterized (by) the high-tech industries of this country.
Sen Sarbanes: "If inflation continues to slow ... won't real short-term interest rates rise?"
Greenspan: "You're quite correct that the real federal funds rate has risen inversely to the fall in the deflator or the CPI, which we would use to do it."
